title: Region tiering and slot-multiplex pilot — weekly notes
content:
Summary:
Quick recap of the region-tiering + slot-multiplex pilot this week. Goal: validate that multiplexing small inference slots (1/4 and 1/2) in select regions reduces tail queuing and unit cost without regressing latency SLO >95th p50/p95 for our smallest hosted models. Focus regions: us-west1 (canary), eu-west3 (secondary).

This week's pulse (metrics snapshot):
- us-west1: average queue time for multiplex slots down 32% week-over-week; sustained utilization up from 62% -> 78%. p95 latency improved 7% but p99 shows intermittent spikes at 3x baseline (investigating).
- eu-west3: utilization up 14%, but coldstart rate increased for 1/4 slots after autoscaler bump at 03:00 UTC on 11/15.
- Cost estimate (pilot window): projected 11% per-token GPU cost reduction when multiplexing is applied for low-seq workloads.

Pilot experiments and observations:
- Multiplex kernel packing: packing 3 short-seq requests onto a single SM block showed good throughput but created jitter when one request had an unexpected long decode pass. Need to add per-request length cap in the router by default.
- Autoscaler interplay: the existing autoscaler treats multiplex slots as identical capacity units; that caused naively-triggered scale-ups. Quick fix: tag multiplex slots with `multiplexed:true` and use separate scale thresholds. PR linked above modifies the scaler to consider effective concurrency.
- KV cache behavior: multiplexed slots share eviction pressure; observed a 12% hit-rate drop for small-model KV caches in us-west1 during 11/14 spike. Hypothesis: multiplexed packing evicts short-lived session keys faster. Potential mitigation: sticky cache buckets per-request-group or soft partitioning.

Anomalies and incidents:
- 2026-11-15 03:04 UTC (eu-west3): burst autoscale added 6 nodes then global rebalancer preempted 2 nodes -> small window where requests landed on higher-latency hosts. Root cause: autoscaler threshold too aggressive for multiplex density change. Action: revert temporary threshold; scheduled follow-up config.
- 11/16 p99 spikes in us-west1 correlated with a rare scheduling conflict (two large decode requests accidentally placed in same multiplex group). We need stricter request classification (length + token budget) at ingress.

Decisions made this week:
- Ship conservative router change that enforces per-request seq_limit=1024 default when multiplexing is enabled. (owners: Priya, Liam)
- Defer global rollout: keep multiplex pilot confined to two regions for another 3 weeks while we validate mitigations for KV cache and autoscaler interactions.
- Add mux-specific autoscaler policy type `mux-conservative` that uses headroom measured in effective concurrent requests rather than node counts. (owner: Evelyn)

Open questions / unknowns:
- Does soft-partitioning of KV caches (per virtual-slot) introduce unacceptable memory overhead at scale? Need memory profile across GPU instance types.
- What is the impact on downstream tracing and billing (token attribution) when requests are packed and share a GPU? Ops wants a clear mapping for chargeback.
- Should we expose a per-customer multiplex opt-in flag (tenant-level) or keep routing purely workload-driven?

Action items / owners (next 7 days):
- Priya: finalize router seq_limit PR + integration tests (due 2026-11-19).
- Liam: run mem-profiling job for multiplex kernels across A10/A100 instances and share heap snapshots (due 2026-11-20).
- Maya: add observability panels for mux-specific KV hit-rate and per-virtual-slot latency (due 2026-11-19).
- Evelyn: prototype `mux-conservative` autoscaler policy and smoke test in staging (due 2026-11-22).
- Arjun (me): draft pilot comms for CS/solutions teams describing expected behavior and opt-in controls (draft by 2026-11-20).

Notes to self / informal items:
- We should add a small synthetic test that occasionally injects a long-decode request into a mux group to measure worst-case jitter — will help set per-request caps.
- Slack convo reference: #gpu-ops thread from 11/16 has flamegraph and kernel traces.

Meeting attendees for weekly sync (2026-11-17): Arjun, Priya, Maya, Liam, Evelyn, Marcus (SRE), Danielle (Obs eng), customer-success rep: Jana.

Next week's plan:
1) Stabilize autoscaler interaction, land `mux-conservative` smoke test.
2) Add router-level classification + tests to reduce accidental mixing of long requests.
3) Run 48-hour extended soak in us-west1 and collect p50/p95/p99 + KV hit-rate + cost delta.
4) Draft decision matrix for rollout gates (KV hit-rate threshold, p99 delta threshold, coldstart delta).

End notes: keeping this intentionally terse — call out anything missing in comments below. If you want deeper kernel-level traces, ask Liam and attach the flamegraph link.

-- Arjun
